Ali: Quick sync — ACME wants a committed throughput proposal. They asked for 1,000,000 tokens/min across two regions with a 99.9% availability and p95 latency budget of 500ms. Need a realistic commit + backstop plan before the SOW.
Sam: Do we have their traffic shape? avg tokens/req and burst fraction?
Marta: Benchmark summary from last quarter: our 13B q8 benchmark yields ~500 tokens/sec per GPU at typical 2k context loads (real numbers vary). That maps to 30k tokens/min per GPU.
Ali: OK using 30k tokens/min/GPU => base GPUs = ceil(1,000,000 / 30,000) = 34 GPUs.
Marta: + we need buffer for headroom and failover. Suggest commit floor = 34 and guaranteed commit = 44 (≈30% buffer). Also plan regional split: primary region 60% / secondary 40% => 26 GPUs primary, 18 GPUs secondary (rounded).
Jay-Product: Is the buffer driven by latency SLO or autoscaling lag? If customers expect sustained commit, burst shouldn’t eat into committed capacity.
Marta: Both. Buffer covers backend overhead (kv cache warming, cold KV load), plus scheduled maintenance. Autoscale warm-up ~ 3–5 minutes for scale-up; we must avoid relying on that for steady-state bursts.
Kevin-Finance: Need monthly committed GPU-hours for billing. Assuming 44 GPUs constant => 44 GPUs * 24h * 30d = 31,680 GPU-hours/month. We'll convert to committed units in quote. Also show an optional 20% burst overlay billed as usage above commit.
Sam: Can we reduce commit size with caching strategies? If many requests share prefixes we can lower steady commit.
Marta: Yes: prefix cache could shave 15–25% token load on typical ACME prompt mix. Conservative estimate -> reduce committed GPUs from 34 to 29 (if cache hit rate ~20%). Recommend we build two pricing scenarios in the SOW: (A) conservative no-cache commit = 44 GPUs reserved (includes buffer); (B) optimized commit w/ caching = 35 GPUs reserved.
Ali: Need to capture region constraints: APAC can't be primary due to VPC peering latency for ACME. So commit will be US-East primary, EU secondary. Any infra limits on min pool per region?
Marta: We require minimum 8 GPUs per region to keep hot pools and failover. Our regional floor means the smallest valid split for ACME is 26/18 as suggested (both >=8). Good.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: ensure commit shows up in billing, create canary pool of 4 GPUs in each region for rollouts.
Kevin-Finance: Add pricing scenarios and delta to monthly invoice. Also flag that committed discount tier depends on 12 vs 36 month term.
Sam: For the SOW I'll document both scenarios plus a playbook for emergency backstop (automated fallback to hosted pool with capacity-based surcharge).
Ali: Action items: Marta to produce formal sizing doc with numbers + test plan, Kevin to draft billing line items for both scenarios, Sam to add SLA and backstop language in SOW. Meeting Friday 10:00 PT to finalize. :thumbsup:
Marta: I'll drop a short spreadsheet with the GPU->token math and regional split in #eng-sre later today. :thumbsup:
